title: Fix Roadblock Detection
eyebrow: Proposal · bug found in the merged roadblocks check (issue #569), nothing built yet

short.lead: The roadblocks check missed the reply on your PC for two reasons I reproduced, and a third I cannot rule out; you choose how strict the repaired check should be.
short.hint: Tap a step to see it.
items: Two bugs reproduced in test runs

I ran the merged check with the claim "I can't verify here". A curly apostrophe (can’t) was not flagged. A turn that ran git ls-files counted as a probe, because the check matches the word ls anywhere in a command.

items.alt: The two ways a claim slips through
items.caption: Both slips were reproduced with the merged code.

items: A session opened before the update may still run the old build
Plugins load when a session starts, and installing an update does not reach a session that is already open. The Castle session had run for 32 minutes. I cannot see which version it loaded from here.

items.caption: An open session keeps the build it started with.

items: You check the install and re-test in a new session
Steps are in Wrap-up. If the new session still lets a claim through, the two bugs above are the cause I can fix.
Your approval is recorded in the decisions log.
Pick options under Your choices, then send the approval line with Copy my reply.

changes: Matches both apostrophes and counts only real probe commands.

Today the pattern needs a straight apostrophe, and any command containing ls, where, npm, pip or apt counts as a probe. After the fix, a command counts only when a probe program starts it, and curly apostrophes match.
Words the Castle reply used that the list lacks.
Today the list has nine phrases such as I can't and not installed. The Castle reply said it could not verify the work here, and that kind of wording is not covered everywhere.
choices: first
How should the check decide a turn really probed?
A
Count a command only when a probe program starts it, such as which, ls, uname, hostname, where or an installer (my suggestion)
Fixes the git ls-files slip with a small change and few wrong blocks.
B
Also require the command to name the thing claimed missing, such as Blender
Strictest, but a wrong guess at the subject would block honest replies.
C
Leave the probe test as it is
Keeps the slip: almost any busy turn passes.
A closes the observed slip without guessing what a reply is about.
second
Which wording should be flagged?
A
Curly apostrophes, plus can't verify, unable to, don't have access, not available here and isn't available (my suggestion)
Covers the Castle reply and its close relatives.
B
Curly apostrophes only
Smallest change; other wordings still slip through.
A adds only phrases that signal a stop, so honest replies are rarely caught.

wrapup.summary: This proposal repairs the roadblocks check so it flags the reply that slipped through on your PC, and asks you to confirm the PC loaded the new version.
wrapup.changing: The roadblock check and its phrase list in core.py, its test cases, and the docs.
wrapup.blocking: Your two picks, and your result from the new-session check.
wrapup.next: After you approve, I plan the fix and build it with test cases.
